clue.text: Hardy return — of the oyster.

explanation.surface: A novelist's homecoming somehow involves shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hardy wrote the novel The Return of the Native, so 'Hardy return' points to the last word of its title; a native is also a cultivated British oyster.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel's title supplies the word after 'return of the', and the same word names an oyster bred in British beds.

clue.text: Joints in a figure, trim and well-finished.

parts.note: a figure is a body's shape
hips are joints of the body

explanation.surface: A description of a body that is neat and nicely toned.
explanation.definitionFit: Something neat, orderly and properly finished is described with this nautical idiom.

clue.text: Open up the refreshment counter?

parts.note: read as un-doing a bar: opening a pub counter is also simply taking the bolt off something

explanation.surface: A publican is asked to start serving drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw back the bolt of a door or gate is to unfasten it, and a pub counter is a bar.

clue.text: The diplomacy employed when one's guests are assembled?

explanation.surface: A host smoothing things over among guests at a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase normally means politics run along factional lines, here read as the politics of a social gathering.

clue.text: Anyhow, some accept these condiments as suiting.

explanation.surface: Seasonings are welcomed, apparently suiting the diner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anyhow, some accept' is padding to the surface. The second sense is cloth: a fabric woven with dark and light flecks is called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The two common table seasonings name it, and so does flecked grey suiting fabric.

clue.text: Always free, this stand.

clue.text: One who does hearken thus may damped.
